title: Christ reveals us (Gaudium et Spes 22)
hook: Christ fully reveals humanity to itself
tomorrow: is the self something you find, or something you give?

segments.voice: Yesterday, conscience: a law we didn't write, heard in the sanctuary of a person, where each one is alone with God.

Personality quizzes. Star signs. A feed that guesses what you'll want before you do. There's no shortage of offers to tell you who you are. Gaudium et Spes has an answer of its own, and it doesn't start with you. It starts with a person. Jewish teachers, in the Mishnah, asked the same question, and answered it with a coin.
screen: `QUIZZES, SIGNS, A FEED THAT GUESSES.` → `IT STARTS WITH A PERSON.` → `AND A COIN.`

segments.voice: The question is old: what is a human being? Paragraph twenty-two answers by looking somewhere unexpected. Christ, it says, by revealing the Father and the Father's love, fully reveals humanity to itself and makes its highest calling clear. Notice the direction: not from us up to God, but from Christ back to us. Then it gets physical. By becoming human, the Son of God has in some way united himself with every person. He worked with human hands, thought with a human mind, acted by human choice, loved with a human heart. And it reaches past the Church's walls: this holds, the text says, for all people of good will, in whose hearts grace works unseen. Here's a neighbor asking the same question. The Mishnah, a collection of Jewish teaching, wonders why God began humanity with one single person. One answer: so that no one could ever say to another, my ancestor was greater than yours. Another: a ruler stamps many coins with one seal and they all come out alike, but God stamped every human with the seal of the first human, and not one is like another. So each person may say, the world was created for my sake. What's shared: every face carries a likeness no one else has, and at the root, no one ranks above anyone. What's honestly different: Catholics read the full meaning of a human being in Christ, God made human. Jewish tradition doesn't hold that God became a man; it reads that worth in the one Creator and the first person he made.
screen: `WHAT IS A HUMAN BEING?` · `CHRIST REVEALS US TO OURSELVES.` · `ONE SEAL, NO TWO COINS ALIKE.` · `SHARED, AND HONESTLY DIFFERENT.` · then, large: `REVEALED TO OURSELVES.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands open on your knees and look at them: the lines, a scar, whatever they did today. The council says Christ worked with hands like these. Then let them rest, palms up, and let your breath be the only work for a while.
Christ reveals us. Gaudium et Spes 22: looking at Christ, people learn who they are meant to be.
Your line: revealed to ourselves. Every face carries a stamp no one else has. Go gently.

chat.says: Lupe told Abuela. then cried "i'm a bad kid" all night. how do i tell a 7-year-old who she is?
options: Tell her Jesus shows who she's made to be: loved, one of a kind. A broken statue can't change that.
Tell her good kids don't break things, so she has to earn back being a good kid now.
Tell her it doesn't matter, nobody cares about an old statue, so just forget it happened.
chat.meaning: Gaudium et Spes 22: Christ reveals to people who they are and what they're called to. One mistake doesn't decide who she is.

Gaudium et Spes.meaning: Vatican II's document on the Church in the modern world

Mishnah.meaning: a collection of Jewish teaching and law

grace.meaning: God's free gift of his life and help

good will.meaning: sincere desire for what is good, whatever a person's faith

notes: Paraphrased from GS 22: Christ, by the revelation of the mystery of the Father and his love, fully reveals man to man himself and makes his supreme calling clear; united in some fashion with every man; worked with human hands, thought with a human mind, acted by human choice, loved with a human heart; holds for all people of good will in whose hearts grace works unseen. Confirm.

UNITY THREAD (wisdom day): Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 paraphrased (no public-domain translation quoted): humanity created from a single person for the sake of peace, so that no one could say 'my father was greater than your father'; a king stamps many coins with one seal and they are all alike, but the King of kings stamped every person with the seal of the first man and none is like another; therefore each must say 'for my sake the world was created'. Please have a Jewish reader confirm the paraphrase and that the framing is fair.
